# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by tools/configdoc from internal/config/types.go. Do not edit; run `make docs-config`. -->

Every key Switchyard's config file accepts, with its type, its default and
what it does. Unknown keys are rejected at load time, and
`switchyard config validate` reports every problem at once. For a
commented example of a complete file, see
[configs/switchyard.example.yaml](../configs/switchyard.example.yaml); for
the compose deployment's file, [deploy/config/switchyard.yaml](../deploy/config/switchyard.yaml).

**Paths.** Keys are written as dotted paths from the top of the file.
`[]` stands for any item of a list (`providers[].id` is the
`id` of each provider) and `<name>` for any key of a map
(`routing.profiles.<name>.min_quality`).

**Defaults.** The default column is the value used when a key is left
out; "-" means none is documented, so the zero value applies (empty, 0 or
false). A default that depends on other keys is described in words.

**References.** Any value can be written as `${VAR}` (a required
environment variable), `${VAR:-default}` or
`${file:/path}`; secrets must be. Settings resolve from the
defaults, then the file and its includes, then the environment overrides
`SWITCHYARD_LISTEN`, `SWITCHYARD_ADMIN_LISTEN` and
`SWITCHYARD_LOG_LEVEL`, then command-line flags.

**Reload.** SIGHUP or `POST /admin/v1/reload` applies a changed file
without a restart, except for these keys and everything under them, which
are reported as `restart_required` and need one: `server.listen`, `server.admin_listen`, `server.max_request_bytes`, `server.max_header_bytes`, `server.read_header_timeout`, `server.body_read_timeout`, `server.write_timeout`, `server.idle_timeout`, `server.shutdown_delay`, `server.shutdown_grace`, `server.tls`, `logging`, `storage`, `telemetry`, `evaluation`, `cache`, `semantic_cache`, `routing.breaker`, `routing.rate_limit_cooldown`, `routing.fallback.retry_budget_ratio`, `routing.fallback.retry_budget_min`. So do the
features a reload turns on that are built only at startup: the semantic
cache (`policies[].cache.semantic`), shadow sampling
(`policies[].shadow.sample_rate`) and, with `storage.mode: redis`, a
response cache when none was on at startup (`policies[].cache`).
Everything else applies at once, `server.admin_token` and the rate limits
included.

## Value types

| Type | Written as |
|---|---|
| byte size | ByteSize is a size in bytes, written in config either as an integer or as a number with a unit: B, KB, MB, GB (powers of 1000) or KiB, MiB, GiB (powers of 1024), for example "10MiB". |
| duration | Duration is a time.Duration written in config as a Go duration string, such as "60s" or "2m30s". |
| decimal | Price is a non-negative decimal amount of USD per million tokens, written as a YAML number or string, for example 0.15 or "0.0375". It keeps the exact decimal text so that cost accounting can avoid float rounding. The zero value means "not set". |
| secret | Secret holds a sensitive value such as an API key, a DSN or a URL that may embed a password. It never reveals its contents when printed, logged or serialized; only Value returns the plaintext. The zero value is an empty secret. |

## Top level

Keys at the top level of the file. Sections that hold further keys link to their own table.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | integer | - | `version` is the schema version. Only 1 is defined, and it is required. |
| `include` | list of strings | - | `include` lists glob patterns of additional files, resolved relative to the directory of the root file. Included files may only define providers, models, aliases and quality_overrides; list entries are appended in sorted file-name order, and a duplicate `id`, or an alias defined twice, in any files, is an error. |
| [`server`](#server) | object | - | `server` configures the public and admin HTTP listeners. |
| [`logging`](#logging) | object | - | `logging` configures the process logger. |
| [`storage`](#storage) | object | - | `storage` selects the state backends: where budgets, rate limits, cache entries and namespace versions live, and the usage ledger. |
| [`providers`](#providers) | list of objects | - | `provider` is an upstream endpoint plus its credentials. |
| [`models`](#models) | list of objects | - | `model` is a logical model in the catalog (DESIGN §16.4). |
| [`tenants`](#tenants) | list of objects | - | `tenants` own the API keys that clients use to call the gateway. With no tenants configured, every /v1 request is rejected with 401. |
| `aliases` | map of string to string | - | `aliases` maps virtual model names to a catalog model `id` or a pinned deployment (model@provider), or the virtual model "auto" or "auto:&lt;profile&gt;" of a defined profile. Alias names follow `model.id` rules and must not collide with a model `id`. |
| [`routing`](#routing) | object | - | `routing` holds gateway-wide routing settings: profiles, fallback and retries, breakers, the assessor and the router's estimates. |
| [`budgets`](#budgets) | object | - | `budgets` holds gateway-wide budget settings. |
| [`policies`](#policies) | list of objects | - | `policies` are referenced by tenants and keys (DESIGN §13). |
| [`quality_overrides`](#quality_overrides) | list of objects | - | `quality_overrides` replace catalog quality priors with measured values, usually written by `switchyard eval fit` into an included file. |
| [`evaluation`](#evaluation) | object | - | `evaluation` configures the judge and shadow sampling. |
| [`cache`](#cache) | object | - | `cache` holds gateway-wide response-cache limits (DESIGN §11). Whether a request is cached is set per policy (`policy.cache`). |
| [`semantic_cache`](#semantic_cache) | object | - | `semantic_cache` configures the embedding model and lookup budget of the semantic cache (DESIGN §11.3). |
| [`rate_limits`](#rate_limits) | object | - | `rate_limits` holds gateway-wide rate-limit settings; the limits themselves are per tenant and key. |
| [`telemetry`](#telemetry) | object | - | `telemetry` configures tracing (DESIGN §15.3). |

## server

`server` configures the public and admin HTTP listeners.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server.listen` | string | `:8080` | `listen` is the public API address (host:port). Default ":8080". |
| `server.admin_listen` | string | `127.0.0.1:9090` | `admin_listen` is the address for /metrics and /admin/v1/*. Default "127.0.0.1:9090". It must never be reachable from the internet. |
| `server.max_request_bytes` | byte size | `10MiB` | `max_request_bytes` caps request bodies; larger bodies get 413. Default 10MiB. |
| `server.max_header_bytes` | byte size | `64KiB` | `max_header_bytes` caps request headers; larger headers get 431. Default 64KiB. net/http allows up to 4 KiB beyond this before it rejects them. |
| `server.read_header_timeout` | duration | `10s` | `read_header_timeout` bounds how long a client may take to send headers. Default 10s. |
| `server.body_read_timeout` | duration | `60s` | `body_read_timeout` bounds how long a client may take to send a request body to an API endpoint; a slower one gets 408. Default 60s. |
| `server.write_timeout` | duration | `60s` | `write_timeout` bounds each write to an API client: a whole JSON response, or one streamed event. A client that stops reading cannot hold its request, and the upstream call behind it, longer. Default 60s. |
| `server.idle_timeout` | duration | `120s` | `idle_timeout` closes idle keep-alive connections. Default 120s. |
| `server.shutdown_delay` | duration | `0s` | `shutdown_delay` is how long the server keeps serving after SIGTERM while /readyz already fails, so load balancers can stop routing to it first. Default 0s. |
| `server.shutdown_grace` | duration | `60s` | `shutdown_grace` bounds how long in-flight requests may take to finish once the listeners have closed. Default 60s. |
| `server.admin_token` | secret | - | `admin_token`, when set, must be sent as "Authorization: Bearer &lt;token&gt;" on every /admin/v1/* route; /metrics and the health routes of the admin listener stay open, for scrapers and probes. It is required when `admin_listen` is not a loopback address. It must be at least 32 characters, without whitespace or control characters (`openssl rand -base64 32` or `switchyard keys generate` make one). Failed admin tokens count against the client address's rate_limits.auth_failures_per_minute, as failed API keys do. |
| `server.tls` | object | - | TLS, when `cert_file` and `key_file` are set, serves the public listener over HTTPS. Both or neither must be set. |
| `server.tls.cert_file` | string | - | `cert_file` is a PEM certificate chain; `key_file` its PEM private key. |
| `server.tls.key_file` | string | - | `cert_file` is a PEM certificate chain; `key_file` its PEM private key. |
| `server.tls.min_version` | string | `1.2` | `min_version` is 1.2 (default) or 1.3. |

## logging

`logging` configures the process logger.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `logging.level` | string | `info` | `level` is one of debug, info, warn, error. Default info. |
| `logging.format` | string | `json` | `format` is json or text. Default json. |

## storage

`storage` selects the state backends: where budgets, rate limits, cache entries and namespace versions live, and the usage ledger.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `storage.mode` | string | `memory` | `mode` is memory (quickstart and dev only; state is lost on restart) or redis. Default memory. |
| `storage.redis` | object | - | RedisStorage holds the two `redis` roles described in DESIGN §11.5. The URLs are secrets because they may embed passwords. |
| `storage.redis.cache_url` | secret | - | `cache_url` is the evictable cache instance (maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru). Required when `storage.mode` is redis. |
| `storage.redis.state_url` | secret | - | `state_url` is the non-evictable state instance (maxmemory-policy noeviction). Required when `storage.mode` is redis. |
| `storage.ledger` | object | - | `ledger` configures where usage events are stored. |
| `storage.ledger.driver` | string | `memory` | `driver` is memory or postgres. Default memory. |
| `storage.ledger.dsn` | secret | - | `dsn` is the Postgres connection string. Required when `driver` is postgres. |
| `storage.ledger.batch_size` | integer | `500` | `batch_size` is the most usage events written in one batch. Default 500. |
| `storage.ledger.flush_interval` | duration | `1s` | `flush_interval` is the longest an event waits before its batch is written. Default 1s. |
| `storage.ledger.queue_size` | integer | `100000` | `queue_size` bounds the in-memory queue of events waiting to be written. When it is full the oldest event is dropped and counted (DESIGN §12.2). Default 100000. |

## providers

`provider` is an upstream endpoint plus its credentials.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `providers[].id` | string | - | `id` names the provider in deployment IDs (model@provider). |
| `providers[].type` | string | - | `type` is the wire protocol: openai (OpenAI and every OpenAI-compatible upstream), anthropic (the Messages API) or gemini (Google's native generateContent API; base_url is the API version root, such as https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta). |
| `providers[].base_url` | string | - | `base_url` is the API root, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1. It must be an absolute http(s) URL and must not embed credentials. |
| `providers[].api_key` | secret | - | `api_key` is the upstream credential. Optional, for self-hosted upstreams. |
| `providers[].tags` | list of strings | - | `tags` are matched by policies, e.g. self_hosted, zdr, region_eu. |
| `providers[].max_concurrency` | integer | - | `max_concurrency` caps in-flight requests per replica; 0 means unlimited. |
| `providers[].forward_headers` | list of strings | - | `forward_headers` lists client headers that may be forwarded upstream. Authorization and Cookie can never be forwarded. |
| `providers[].timeouts` | object | - | ProviderTimeouts bound each upstream call. |
| `providers[].timeouts.connect` | duration | `5s` | `connect` bounds TCP and TLS connection setup. Default 5s. |
| `providers[].timeouts.first_token` | duration | `30s` | `first_token` bounds a stream's wait for its first event. It applies to streams only: a non-streaming response arrives only after the whole generation, so `total` and the request's deadline bound it instead. Default 30s. |
| `providers[].timeouts.idle` | duration | `60s` | `idle` bounds the gap between streamed chunks, measured only while the gateway waits for the upstream, not while it writes to its client. Default 60s. |
| `providers[].timeouts.total` | duration | `10m` | `total` bounds the whole upstream call, including the full streamed response. Default 10m. |

## models

`model` is a logical model in the catalog (DESIGN §16.4).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `models[].id` | string | - | `id` is the name clients send in the model field. It must not contain "@" and must not be "auto" or start with "auto:", which are reserved for virtual models. |
| `models[].type` | string | `chat` | `type` is chat (default) or embedding. Chat models serve /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions; embedding models serve /v1/embeddings. |
| `models[].context_window` | integer | - | `context_window` is the maximum number of input plus output tokens. 0 means unknown, which disables the context-size filter for this model. |
| `models[].max_output_tokens` | integer | - | `max_output_tokens` is the most the model can generate in one response. Adapters that require max_tokens (Anthropic) use it as the default. 0 means unknown. |
| `models[].capabilities` | list of strings | - | `capabilities` lists what the model supports, from a fixed vocabulary: streaming, stream_usage, tools, parallel_tools, forced_tools, vision, json_mode, json_schema, n, logprobs, seed, sampling, temperature_2, penalties, completions, prompt_caching. json_schema means native structured-output support: no deployment emulates it. A request needing a capability that a deployment lacks is never sent to it (DESIGN §6.2, §9.2), unless the parameters that need it are dropped (`routing`). |
| `models[].quality` | map of string to number | - | `quality` holds quality priors in [0, 1] per category: general, coding, reasoning, extraction, creative, tool_use (DESIGN §10.2), used by cost-aware routing; quality_overrides can replace them. |
| `models[].token_ratio` | number | - | `token_ratio` scales the bytes/4 token estimate for this model's tokenizer. 0 means 1. |
| `models[].dimensions` | integer | - | `dimensions` is the vector size of an embedding model. |
| `models[].deployments` | list of objects | - | `deployments` lists the providers that serve this model. At least one is required, and each provider may appear at most once per model. |
| `models[].deployments[].provider` | string | - | `provider` references `provider.id`. |
| `models[].deployments[].upstream_model` | string | - | `upstream_model` is the model name sent to the provider. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing` | object | - | `pricing` is what this deployment costs. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.input` | decimal | - | `input` is the price of input tokens that are not read from a cache. Every price is in USD per million tokens; one that is not set is unknown. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.output` | decimal | - | `output` is the price of output tokens. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.cached_input` | decimal | - | `cached_input` is the price of input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache (a cache hit). |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.cache_write` | decimal | - | `cache_write` is the price of input tokens written to the cache, where the provider charges one per token. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.source` | string | - | `source` is the URL the prices were checked against. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.checked` | string | - | `checked` is the date the prices were last checked, as YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes` | list of objects | - | `changes` are announced price changes, in strictly increasing from order. Each replaces the prices it gives, from its from time on; a price it omits keeps its value from before the change. The catalog resolves the prices in force whenever the gateway builds its snapshot, and the gateway rebuilds it at each change, so costs, budgets and routing switch on time without a reload. `switchyard catalog lint` notes the next change and changes already in force, which belong in the prices above. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes[].from` | string | - | `from` is when the change takes effect: a date as YYYY-MM-DD, which means 00:00 UTC, or an RFC 3339 timestamp with its offset, such as 2026-12-01T00:00:00-08:00, for a provider that names a time zone. Required. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes[].input` | decimal | - | `input`, when set, is the input price from `from` on; unset keeps the one in force before the change. `output`, `cached_input` and `cache_write` work the same way. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes[].output` | decimal | - | `output`, when set, is the output price from `from` on. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes[].cached_input` | decimal | - | `cached_input`, when set, is the cache-read price from `from` on. |
| `models[].deployments[].pricing.changes[].cache_write` | decimal | - | `cache_write`, when set, is the cache-write price from `from` on. |
| `models[].deployments[].capabilities` | list of strings | - | `capabilities`, when set, replaces the model's list for this deployment (for example a host that lacks parallel tool calls). |
| `models[].deployments[].tags` | list of strings | - | `tags` are added to the provider's tags for this deployment. |
| `models[].deployments[].quality_offset` | number | - | `quality_offset` adjusts the model's quality priors for this deployment, e.g. -0.02 for a quantized variant. Must be in [-1, 1]. |
| `models[].deployments[].latency_hint` | object | - | `latency_hint` seeds latency estimates until there are measurements. |
| `models[].deployments[].latency_hint.ttft_ms` | integer | - | `ttft_ms` is the typical time to first token, in milliseconds. |
| `models[].deployments[].latency_hint.tokens_per_sec` | number | - | `tokens_per_sec` is the typical output speed. |

## tenants

`tenants` own the API keys that clients use to call the gateway. With no tenants configured, every /v1 request is rejected with 401.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tenants[].id` | string | - | `id` names the tenant in logs and reports. Same rules as `provider.id`. |
| `tenants[].keys` | list of objects | - | `keys` are the gateway API keys that authenticate as this tenant. |
| `tenants[].keys[].id` | string | - | `id` names the key in logs and reports (never the key itself). It must be unique across all tenants. Same rules as `provider.id`. |
| `tenants[].keys[].hash` | string | - | `hash` is "sha256:" followed by 64 lowercase hex characters: the SHA-256 of the full plaintext key. Hashes must be unique across all tenants. |
| `tenants[].keys[].tags` | list of strings | - | `tags` are matched by policy rules (key_tags), e.g. prod, eu. |
| `tenants[].keys[].policy` | string | - | `policy`, when set, overrides the tenant's policy for this key. |
| `tenants[].keys[].rate_limit` | object (optional) | - | `rate_limit`, when set, replaces the tenant's rate_limit for this key. |
| `tenants[].keys[].rate_limit.requests_per_minute` | integer | - | `requests_per_minute` is the sustained request rate, enforced with GCRA. 0 means unlimited. |
| `tenants[].keys[].rate_limit.burst` | integer | `requests_per_minute` / 6 (ten seconds' worth), at least 1 | `burst` is how many requests may arrive at once on top of the sustained rate. Default: `requests_per_minute` / 6 (ten seconds' worth), at least 1. |
| `tenants[].keys[].rate_limit.max_concurrent_streams` | integer | - | `max_concurrent_streams` caps the key's in-flight streaming requests. 0 means unlimited. |
| `tenants[].budgets` | list of objects | - | `budgets` cap this tenant's spend (DESIGN §12.3). A budget with scope key applies to each of the tenant's keys separately. |
| `tenants[].budgets[].scope` | string | - | `scope` is tenant (the tenant's total spend) or key (each key's spend). |
| `tenants[].budgets[].window` | string | - | `window` is day or month, as calendar periods in UTC. |
| `tenants[].budgets[].limit_usd` | decimal | - | `limit_usd` is the cap, in USD, as an exact decimal (for example "2000"). |
| `tenants[].budgets[].soft_at` | number | - | `soft_at`, when set, is a fraction in (0, 1) of the limit. Crossing it is logged and counted once per window, and with `soft_profile` it downgrades "auto" requests. |
| `tenants[].budgets[].on_exhausted` | string | `block` | `on_exhausted` is block (requests that would exceed the limit get 429 budget_exceeded) or notify (they are served, logged and counted). Default block. |
| `tenants[].budgets[].soft_profile` | string | - | `soft_profile`, when set with `soft_at`, is the profile "auto" requests use once the soft threshold has been crossed in the current window. |
| `tenants[].policy` | string | - | `policy` names the tenant's policy. Empty means the policy with `id` "default" if one exists, otherwise built-in defaults. |
| `tenants[].rate_limit` | object | - | `rate_limit` applies to each of the tenant's keys separately, unless the key sets its own. The zero value means no limit. |
| `tenants[].rate_limit.requests_per_minute` | integer | - | `requests_per_minute` is the sustained request rate, enforced with GCRA. 0 means unlimited. |
| `tenants[].rate_limit.burst` | integer | `requests_per_minute` / 6 (ten seconds' worth), at least 1 | `burst` is how many requests may arrive at once on top of the sustained rate. Default: `requests_per_minute` / 6 (ten seconds' worth), at least 1. |
| `tenants[].rate_limit.max_concurrent_streams` | integer | - | `max_concurrent_streams` caps the key's in-flight streaming requests. 0 means unlimited. |

## routing

`routing` holds gateway-wide routing settings: profiles, fallback and retries, breakers, the assessor and the router's estimates.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `routing.drop_unsupported_params` | boolean | `false` | `drop_unsupported_params` lets a request reach a deployment that cannot honor some optional parameters (n, logprobs, seed, penalties, temperature above 1, parallel tool calls) by removing them, instead of excluding the deployment. Default false. temperature and top_p are removed for a deployment without capability sampling whatever this says. |
| `routing.request_timeout` | duration | `10m` | `request_timeout` is the whole-request deadline, across every attempt, backoff and the full streamed response. A client's X-Switchyard-Timeout-Ms header can only lower it. Default 10m. |
| `routing.fallback` | object | - | `fallback` bounds retries and fallback plans (DESIGN §14.2, §14.3). |
| `routing.fallback.max_deployments` | integer | `3` | `max_deployments` is the plan length: the primary deployment plus its fallbacks, 1 to 10. Default 3. |
| `routing.fallback.retries_per_deployment` | integer | `1` | `retries_per_deployment` is how many times a deployment is retried after a retryable failure before the next one is tried, 0 to 5. Default 1. |
| `routing.fallback.backoff_base` | duration | - | `backoff_base` and `backoff_max` shape the exponential backoff with full jitter before retry n: a random sleep in [0, min(max, base×2^n)]. Defaults 250ms and 2s. |
| `routing.fallback.backoff_max` | duration | - | `backoff_base` and `backoff_max` shape the exponential backoff with full jitter before retry n: a random sleep in [0, min(max, base×2^n)]. Defaults 250ms and 2s. |
| `routing.fallback.retry_budget_ratio` | number | `0.2` | `retry_budget_ratio` caps the retries to one deployment at this fraction of its requests over a sliding 10 s window, in (0, 1]. Default 0.2. |
| `routing.fallback.retry_budget_min` | integer | `5` | `retry_budget_min` is the number of retries per window that are always allowed, whatever the ratio says. Default 5. |
| `routing.breaker` | object | - | `breaker` configures the per-deployment circuit breakers (§14.4). |
| `routing.breaker.consecutive_failures` | integer | `5` | `consecutive_failures`, default 5. |
| `routing.breaker.failure_ratio` | number | `0.5` | `failure_ratio`, in (0, 1]. Default 0.5. |
| `routing.breaker.min_requests` | integer | `20` | `min_requests`, default 20. |
| `routing.breaker.window` | duration | `30s` | `window`, default 30s. |
| `routing.breaker.open_for` | duration | `30s` | `open_for`, default 30s. |
| `routing.breaker.half_open_probes` | integer | `3` | `half_open_probes`, default 3. |
| `routing.rate_limit_cooldown` | object | - | `rate_limit_cooldown` is how long a deployment is skipped after a 429. |
| `routing.rate_limit_cooldown.default` | duration | `1s` | Default applies to a 429 without Retry-After. Default 1s. |
| `routing.rate_limit_cooldown.max` | duration | `30s` | `max` caps the cooldown. Default 30s. |
| `routing.stream_keepalive` | duration | 0s (off) | `stream_keepalive`, when positive, commits a streaming response that has not received its first upstream event after this long: the gateway sends 200, the SSE headers and a ": keep-alive" comment, repeated at this interval until the first event. After the first keep-alive no fallback is possible, and a failure becomes an error event in the stream. Default 0s (off). |
| `routing.default_profile` | string | `balanced` | `default_profile` is the profile used when a policy names none and for plain "auto". Default "balanced". |
| `routing.profiles` | map of string to object | - | `profiles` are routing objectives plus constraints, selected with model "auto:&lt;name&gt;" (DESIGN §9.3). When none are configured the built-in cheap, balanced, quality and fast profiles apply. |
| `routing.profiles.<name>.min_quality` | number | - | `min_quality` is the quality bar in [0, 1] (DESIGN §10.4). |
| `routing.profiles.<name>.objective` | string | `cost` | `objective` is cost (cheapest eligible) or latency (fastest eligible by estimated time to first token). Default cost. |
| `routing.profiles.<name>.max_ttft_ms` | integer | - | `max_ttft_ms`, when &gt; 0, is a soft latency target in milliseconds. |
| `routing.expected_output_tokens` | integer | `500` | `expected_output_tokens` is the output estimate when a request sets no max_tokens. Default 500. |
| `routing.assessor` | object | - | `assessor` configures request difficulty assessment (DESIGN §10.3). |
| `routing.assessor.type` | string | `heuristic` | `type` is heuristic, the only kind so far. Default heuristic. |
| `routing.assessor.weights` | map of string to number | - | `weights` overrides the heuristic's signal weights by signal name; see internal/quality for the names and defaults. |

## budgets

`budgets` holds gateway-wide budget settings.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `budgets.fail_mode` | string | `open` | `fail_mode` decides what happens when the budget store is unavailable: open (serve, still enforcing per-request caps, and alert) or closed (reject with 503). Default open. |

## policies

`policies` are referenced by tenants and keys (DESIGN §13).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `policies[].id` | string | - | `id` names the policy. Same rules as `provider.id`. |
| `policies[].profile` | string | - | `profile` is the default profile for "auto" requests. Empty means routing.default_profile. |
| `policies[].allowed_profiles` | list of strings | - | `allowed_profiles` lists the profiles callers may select by model name or header. Empty means all. |
| `policies[].allow` | list of strings | - | `allow` and `deny` are glob patterns over deployment IDs (model@provider). Empty `allow` means allow all; `deny` wins over `allow`. |
| `policies[].deny` | list of strings | - | `allow` and `deny` are glob patterns over deployment IDs (model@provider). Empty `allow` means allow all; `deny` wins over `allow`. |
| `policies[].prefer` | list of strings | - | `prefer` lists ordered globs; earlier patterns form higher preference tiers, and cost decides within a tier. |
| `policies[].require_tags` | list of strings | - | `require_tags`: a deployment must carry all of these tags (provider tags plus deployment tags). |
| `policies[].substitution` | object | - | `substitution` says whether a concrete model name may be served by a different model. |
| `policies[].substitution.mode` | string | `pinned` | `mode` is pinned (only the requested model) or equivalent. Default pinned. |
| `policies[].substitution.max_quality_drop` | number | `0.05` | `max_quality_drop` is how far below the requested model's estimate a substitute may be, in [0, 1]. Default 0.05. |
| `policies[].routing_mode` | string | `enforce` | `routing_mode` is enforce or observe. Default enforce. |
| `policies[].baseline_model` | string | - | `baseline_model` is the savings baseline for "auto" requests and the model served for them in observe mode. Required when auto is allowed. |
| `policies[].max_cost_per_request_usd` | decimal | - | `max_cost_per_request_usd` is a hard cap on a request's estimated cost. |
| `policies[].on_unmet` | string | `best_effort` | `on_unmet` is best_effort or reject: what happens when no candidate meets the soft constraints (quality, latency). Default best_effort. |
| `policies[].rules` | list of objects | - | `rules` are evaluated in order; the first whose match holds applies its set. |
| `policies[].rules[].name` | string | - | Rule is one policy rule. |
| `policies[].rules[].match` | object | - | RuleMatch holds when every condition that is set holds. An empty match is unconditional. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.model` | string | - | `model` is a glob over the requested model name. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.profile` | string | - | `profile` matches the requested profile. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.task` | string | - | `task` matches the assessed (or hinted) category. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.difficulty_gte` | number | - | `difficulty_gte` and `difficulty_lt` bound the assessed difficulty; 0 means unset. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.difficulty_lt` | number | - | `difficulty_gte` and `difficulty_lt` bound the assessed difficulty; 0 means unset. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.key` | string | - | `key` matches the API key `id`; `key_tags` requires all of these key tags. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.key_tags` | list of strings | - | `key` matches the API key `id`; `key_tags` requires all of these key tags. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.header` | map of string to string | - | `header` maps a header name to a glob its value must match. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.tags` | map of string to string | - | `tags` maps an X-Switchyard-Tags key to a glob its value must match. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.stream` | string | - | `stream`, `has_tools` and `has_images` are "true" or "false"; empty means either. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.has_tools` | string | - | `stream`, `has_tools` and `has_images` are "true" or "false"; empty means either. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.has_images` | string | - | `stream`, `has_tools` and `has_images` are "true" or "false"; empty means either. |
| `policies[].rules[].match.est_input_tokens_gte` | integer | - | `est_input_tokens_gte` matches requests at least this large; 0 means unset. |
| `policies[].rules[].set` | object | - | PolicyOverride is what a rule sets. Zero values and nil slices mean "keep the policy's value". |
| `policies[].rules[].set.profile` | string | - | `profile` is the default profile for "auto" requests. Empty means routing.default_profile. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.min_quality` | number | - | `min_quality` is the quality bar in [0, 1] (DESIGN §10.4). |
| `policies[].rules[].set.prefer` | list of strings | - | `prefer` lists ordered globs; earlier patterns form higher preference tiers, and cost decides within a tier. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.allow` | list of strings | - | `allow` and `deny` are glob patterns over deployment IDs (model@provider). Empty `allow` means allow all; `deny` wins over `allow`. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.deny` | list of strings | - | PolicyOverride is what a rule sets. Zero values and nil slices mean "keep the policy's value". |
| `policies[].rules[].set.require_tags` | list of strings | - | `require_tags`: a deployment must carry all of these tags (provider tags plus deployment tags). |
| `policies[].rules[].set.substitution` | object | - | `substitution` says whether a concrete model name may be served by a different model. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.substitution.mode` | string | `pinned` | `mode` is pinned (only the requested model) or equivalent. Default pinned. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.substitution.max_quality_drop` | number | `0.05` | `max_quality_drop` is how far below the requested model's estimate a substitute may be, in [0, 1]. Default 0.05. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.routing_mode` | string | `enforce` | `routing_mode` is enforce or observe. Default enforce. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.max_cost_per_request_usd` | decimal | - | `max_cost_per_request_usd` is a hard cap on a request's estimated cost. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.on_unmet` | string | `best_effort` | `on_unmet` is best_effort or reject: what happens when no candidate meets the soft constraints (quality, latency). Default best_effort. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache` | object (optional) | - | `cache`, when set, replaces the policy's whole cache block (with the same defaults). Only governance rules may set it. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.exact` | object | - | ExactCachePolicy configures the exact cache (DESIGN §11.2). |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.exact.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the exact cache on. Default false. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.exact.ttl` | duration | `24h` | `ttl` is how long an entry is served. Default 24h. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.exact.scope` | string | `tenant` | `scope` is tenant (default), key or user: who shares entries. user scopes by the request's user field, within the tenant; a request without one is scoped by its key. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.exact.deterministic_only` | boolean | - | `deterministic_only` restricts caching to requests with temperature 0 or a seed, so that sampled requests always get a fresh answer. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.semantic` | object | - | SemanticCachePolicy configures the semantic cache (DESIGN §11.3). It shares the exact cache's scope. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.semantic.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the semantic cache on. Default false. It requires semantic_cache.embedding_model. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.semantic.min_similarity` | number | `0.95` | `min_similarity` is the cosine similarity a match needs, in (0, 1]. Default 0.95. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.semantic.ttl` | duration | `72h` | `ttl` is how long an entry is served. Default 72h. |
| `policies[].rules[].set.cache.semantic.max_chars` | integer | `2000` | `max_chars` is the longest last user message eligible, in characters. Default 2000. |
| `policies[].shadow` | object | - | `shadow` configures shadow sampling for this policy's traffic. It is off unless `sample_rate` &gt; 0. |
| `policies[].shadow.sample_rate` | number | - | `sample_rate` is the fraction of eligible requests sampled, in [0, 1]. |
| `policies[].cache` | object | - | `cache` configures the response caches for this policy's chat requests (DESIGN §11). Both caches are off unless enabled. |
| `policies[].cache.exact` | object | - | ExactCachePolicy configures the exact cache (DESIGN §11.2). |
| `policies[].cache.exact.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the exact cache on. Default false. |
| `policies[].cache.exact.ttl` | duration | `24h` | `ttl` is how long an entry is served. Default 24h. |
| `policies[].cache.exact.scope` | string | `tenant` | `scope` is tenant (default), key or user: who shares entries. user scopes by the request's user field, within the tenant; a request without one is scoped by its key. |
| `policies[].cache.exact.deterministic_only` | boolean | - | `deterministic_only` restricts caching to requests with temperature 0 or a seed, so that sampled requests always get a fresh answer. |
| `policies[].cache.semantic` | object | - | SemanticCachePolicy configures the semantic cache (DESIGN §11.3). It shares the exact cache's scope. |
| `policies[].cache.semantic.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns the semantic cache on. Default false. It requires semantic_cache.embedding_model. |
| `policies[].cache.semantic.min_similarity` | number | `0.95` | `min_similarity` is the cosine similarity a match needs, in (0, 1]. Default 0.95. |
| `policies[].cache.semantic.ttl` | duration | `72h` | `ttl` is how long an entry is served. Default 72h. |
| `policies[].cache.semantic.max_chars` | integer | `2000` | `max_chars` is the longest last user message eligible, in characters. Default 2000. |

## quality_overrides

`quality_overrides` replace catalog quality priors with measured values, usually written by `switchyard eval fit` into an included file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quality_overrides[].model` | string | - | `model` is a catalog model `id`. |
| `quality_overrides[].category` | string | - | `category` is a quality category (general, coding, reasoning, extraction, creative, tool_use). |
| `quality_overrides[].value` | number | - | `value` replaces the catalog prior, in [0, 1]. |
| `quality_overrides[].ci_low` | number | - | `ci_low` and `ci_high` bound `value`'s confidence interval, in [0, 1]. |
| `quality_overrides[].ci_high` | number | - | `ci_low` and `ci_high` bound `value`'s confidence interval, in [0, 1]. |
| `quality_overrides[].samples` | integer | - | `samples` is the number of judged comparisons behind `value`. |
| `quality_overrides[].evaluated` | string | - | `evaluated` is the date of the evaluation, as YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `quality_overrides[].source` | string | - | `source` describes the evaluation, e.g. the prompt set and judge model. |

## evaluation

`evaluation` configures the judge and shadow sampling.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `evaluation.judge` | object | - | `judge` is the deployment that compares answers. |
| `evaluation.judge.model` | string | - | `model` is a catalog chat model `id` or model@provider. Required when any policy enables shadow sampling. |
| `evaluation.shadow` | object | - | `shadow` holds gateway-wide shadow-sampling limits. |
| `evaluation.shadow.daily_budget_usd` | decimal | - | `daily_budget_usd` caps the combined cost of shadow and judge calls per tenant per UTC day. Required when any policy enables shadow sampling. |
| `evaluation.shadow.concurrency` | integer | `4` | `concurrency` caps in-flight shadow evaluations per replica. Default 4. |
| `evaluation.shadow.max_output_tokens` | integer | `1024` | `max_output_tokens` caps each shadow and judge completion. Default 1024. |
| `evaluation.shadow.verified_min_samples` | integer | `30` | `verified_min_samples` is how many judged samples a category needs before its savings count as verified. Default 30. |
| `evaluation.shadow.verified_min_pass_rate` | number | `0.9` | `verified_min_pass_rate` is the lower confidence bound the pass rate must reach for verified savings, in (0, 1]. Default 0.9. |

## cache

`cache` holds gateway-wide response-cache limits (DESIGN §11). Whether a request is cached is set per policy (`policy.cache`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cache.lookup_timeout` | duration | `25ms` | `lookup_timeout` bounds an exact-cache lookup (namespace version and entry); a lookup that takes longer is a miss. Default 25ms. |
| `cache.max_entry_bytes` | integer | `1MiB` | `max_entry_bytes` caps a cached response body; larger responses are not cached. Default 1MiB. |
| `cache.memory_max_entries` | integer | `10000` | `memory_max_entries` caps each in-memory cache (storage.mode memory), which evicts the least recently used entry. Default 10000. |

## semantic_cache

`semantic_cache` configures the embedding model and lookup budget of the semantic cache (DESIGN §11.3).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `semantic_cache.embedding_model` | string | - | `embedding_model` is the catalog embedding model, or model@provider, that embeds last user messages. Required when any policy enables the semantic cache. The message is sent to that deployment. |
| `semantic_cache.lookup_timeout` | duration | `150ms` | `lookup_timeout` bounds the embedding and the vector search together; a lookup that takes longer is a miss. Default 150ms. |

## rate_limits

`rate_limits` holds gateway-wide rate-limit settings; the limits themselves are per tenant and key.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rate_limits.fail_mode` | string | `open` | `fail_mode` decides what happens when the rate-limit store is unavailable: open (serve, and alert; default) or closed (reject with 503). |
| `rate_limits.auth_failures_per_minute` | integer | `30` | `auth_failures_per_minute` caps failed authentications per client IP; once exceeded, that IP gets 429 whatever key it sends. Default 30; -1 disables the limit. |

## telemetry

`telemetry` configures tracing (DESIGN §15.3).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `telemetry.tracing` | object | - | `tracing` configures OpenTelemetry traces, exported over OTLP/HTTP (protobuf). Switchyard accepts a W3C traceparent from clients either way; spans are recorded and exported only when `enabled`. |
| `telemetry.tracing.enabled` | boolean | `false` | `enabled` turns tracing on. Default false. |
| `telemetry.tracing.endpoint` | secret | - | `endpoint` is the collector's OTLP/HTTP base URL, for example http://otel-collector:4318; traces are posted to &lt;endpoint&gt;/v1/traces. Required when `enabled`. It may hold credentials, so it is a secret. |
| `telemetry.tracing.sample_ratio` | number | `0.05` | `sample_ratio` is the fraction of new traces sampled, in [0, 1]; a request that arrives with a sampled parent is always sampled (parent-based), so clients control sampling, and the trace `id` of their requests' spans and log lines, through the traceparent they send. Default 0.05. |
| `telemetry.tracing.service_name` | string | `switchyard` | `service_name` is the service.name resource attribute. Default switchyard. |
| `telemetry.tracing.propagate_upstream` | boolean | `false` | `propagate_upstream` sends the W3C traceparent of the gateway's upstream attempt span to providers, only with tracing enabled; tracestate and baggage are never sent, and nor is a client's own trace context. Default false: provider calls leave the trust boundary. |
